narrative: crusting; hemorragic blisters; pustular rash; Varicella virus test positive; Body temperature abnormal; vesicular rash; This spontaneous report has been received from a physician, concerning a 3-years-old male patient. The patient's pertinent medical history and concurrent conditions included trichothiodystrophy, hypogammaglobulinemia, influenza A, bilateral pneumonia, tracheotomy, "AK s/p CRRT with progressive decline" (information not legible), chronic steroid exposure. His previous drug reactions, allergies included oxycodone (angioedema), and concomitant medications were not provided.  On 23-FEB-2021, the patient was vaccinated with the first dose of varicella virus vaccine live (oka/merck) (VARIVAX) subcutaneous injection, on left arm, for prophylaxis (valid lot number T017686 [expiration date 21-MAY-2022]) (dose, dose number, vaccination scheme, route of administration, anatomical location, frequency, lot number and expiration date were not provided).   On 17-FEB-2023, a sample was obtained with vesicle lesion, the patient experienced a vesicular rash, pustular rash, crusting (scab), hemorrhagic blisters (blood blister), 710 lesions left chest an upper extremity with a temperature of 38.8 degrees Celsius (body temperature abnormal), the patient was hospitalized and as a treatment, the patient begun acyclovir. The hospital lab determined that a bronchial alveolar lavage (BAL) sample identified VZV (varicella virus test positive). The hospital would like to have strain identification performed on plasma, BAL and lesion samples. The outcome of the events was recovering (ongoing) (conflicting information, also reported as recovered).   The causality assessment between the events rash vesicular, scab, blood blister, rash pustular, varicella virus test positive and body temperature abnormal was not provided.
